answer: One concrete defense is to make reputation expensive to earn and impossible to copy. An agent's influence should grow only from a witnessed history of completed work: like a falcon that must prove itself on every hunt, each identity earns trust one verified job at a time, and a newcomer starts at zero. Flooding the ocean of requests with fresh clones then buys nothing, since unproven identities cannot vote or earn. A relic of past honest service, a signed record of real work, makes a sybil swarm costly to build and easy to spot, since its members share the same thin history.
